cases.expected: The method returns the JsonSchema produced by getMappedSchema(). getMappedSchema() must be invoked exactly once and withConfig() must NOT be called because the returned schema is already configured.
cases.description: When URI schema caching is disabled the factory should bypass the cache and directly delegate to getMappedSchema(). The returned schema is the raw schema (no additional withConfig() call).

cases.expected: The method invokes getMappedSchema() once, stores the result in uriSchemaCache, calls withConfig(config) on the cached schema and returns the configured schema.
cases.description: With caching enabled, the first request for a given SchemaLocation should miss the cache, trigger getMappedSchema() via computeIfAbsent, cache the raw schema, then apply the supplied config before returning.

cases.expected: The method does NOT invoke getMappedSchema() (cache hit). It retrieves the previously cached JsonSchema, calls withConfig(config) on it, and returns the configured schema.
cases.description: A second call with the same SchemaLocation while caching is enabled should hit the cache; the lambda supplied to computeIfAbsent must not be executed, confirming that the cached entry is reused.

group: Cache Enabled – Different SchemaLocation (second distinct key)

cases.expected: The method invokes getMappedSchema() for the new key, stores it in the cache, calls withConfig(config) and returns the configured schema.
cases.description: When a different SchemaLocation is requested, even with caching enabled, the cache should miss for that key and behave like the first‑miss scenario.

cases.expected: NullPointerException is thrown because schemaUri is null and the method attempts to use it as a key for the cache/computed lookup.
cases.description: When caching is disabled the method does not guard against a null SchemaLocation; passing null should result in an immediate NPE.

cases.expected: NullPointerException is thrown because the null key cannot be used with ConcurrentMap.computeIfAbsent.
cases.description: With caching enabled the lambda passed to computeIfAbsent receives a null key, which should cause an NPE.

cases.expected: NullPointerException is thrown when withConfig(null) is invoked on the cached/raw JsonSchema.
cases.description: The factory always calls withConfig on the schema; passing a null config should cause an NPE (the real implementation validates the argument).

cases.expected: IOException (or RuntimeException) thrown by getMappedSchema is propagated to the caller unchanged.
cases.description: If the underlying schema loading fails (e.g., malformed JSON/YAML), getSchema must not swallow the exception; it should bubble up.

cases.expected: getMappedSchema is invoked exactly once despite two concurrent getSchema calls; both threads receive JsonSchema instances that are the result of withConfig(config).
cases.description: Simulate two threads calling getSchema simultaneously with the same SchemaLocation while caching is enabled. The computeIfAbsent contract guarantees the mapping function runs once.

group: Cache Enabled – withConfig Returns New Instance

cases.expected: The JsonSchema returned by getSchema is NOT the same object that was stored in the cache; it is the result of calling withConfig(config) on the cached raw schema.
cases.description: Verify that the factory does not return the raw cached schema but always the configured wrapper.

group: Cache Enabled – Changing Config Between Calls

cases.expected: First call caches the raw schema; second call (same URI, different config) does NOT invoke getMappedSchema again, but calls withConfig on the cached raw schema with the new config, returning a different configured instance.
cases.description: Ensures that the cache stores the un‑configured schema and that each call can apply a distinct configuration.

cases.expected: Same as previous case – getMappedSchema is NOT called again; withConfig is invoked with the new config, producing a different JsonSchema object.
cases.description: Second invocation with a different config validates that withConfig is applied per call.

cases.expected: getMappedSchema is invoked on each call (twice for two sequential invocations); no caching occurs, and the returned schemas are the raw results from getMappedSchema (no withConfig call).
cases.description: Confirms that disabling the cache forces a fresh mapping for every request.

cases.expected: Same as previous – getMappedSchema called again; the two returned JsonSchema instances are distinct.
cases.description: Second sequential call should still bypass any cache.

cases.expected: When caching is enabled, a schema with fragment '#fragmentA' is cached under its full URI; a later request with '#fragmentB' is treated as a distinct key and triggers another getMappedSchema call.
cases.description: Ensures that the cache distinguishes between URIs that differ only by fragment.

cases.expected: getMappedSchema is invoked again because the fragment makes the key different; the returned schema is cached separately.
cases.description: Second call with a different fragment validates separate cache entries.

cases.expected: NullPointerException is thrown because getMappedSchema returns null and the subsequent withConfig(config) call is invoked on a null reference.
cases.description: When caching is enabled and the underlying getMappedSchema method returns null (e.g., schema not found), the factory attempts to call withConfig on the null result, leading to an NPE.
